methods: Once you understand the basics of a topic, stop watching and build. Pick from the project ideas list and ship something small every week.
For every hour of course material, spend four building. Courses feel productive; shipped code is the evidence.
Take each module quiz without notes. Getting it wrong first and then reading the explanation sticks better than rereading.
Retake a passed quiz after 7 days, then 30. The portal flags them on your Today page.
End each session with a commit, even a small one. Your GitHub history becomes proof of consistency.
Stuck for 30 minutes? Write down what you tried, then ask a forum or an AI tutor. Never stay stuck for an evening.
Write the code yourself first, then ask an assistant to review it. Generated code you can't explain fails interviews.
A short note per module in your log repo or on LinkedIn. It's how recruiters find you before you apply.
